newsitem.title: UK: Thinly supplied NWE straight-run keeps its vigour.
newsitem.headline: Thinly supplied NWE straight-run keeps its vigour.

text.p: Euro straight-run markets maintained their vigour on Thursday, with low sulphur cargoes not available until late August and highly priced, traders said.
German and British refiners talked of having good quality barrels on offer in third decade August, with the German refinery seeking $115 fob for his material.

"We're still at $115 and people are discussing it but nothing is decided yet," the seller said. Others said the price was too high, given crude's fall since Wednesday, but acknowledged a buyer with prompt needs had few choices.
Russian straight-run premia have dropped to more sustainable levels, encouraging solid trade.
M100 straight-run changed hands at two means plus $4 on Wednesday and at plus $5 on Thursday, though buyers were resisting ambitious plus $6 and $7 offers from one French seller.
"Everything that the Russians bring out just gets picked up," said one potential buyer. "It might come off a little but it is just not going to collapse."
